title: Outage Desk and Dispatch Rule — Outage and Trouble Reports on Electric Service by Rate Schedule
content:
1. **Reporting.** Reporting an outage or trouble on an Electric Service by Rate Schedule account is always free and is taken through any report channel.
2. **One report per incident.** A report is attached to the outage management incident number the system assigns; a second report from the same service account for the same incident number is not recorded as a new report.
3. **Safety calls.** Reports of a line down or a tree on the line are dispatched as safety calls and are never charged.
4. **Member-side findings.** When the crew's finding is member side, a trouble call charge is billed — the schedule's business-hours figure when the crew was dispatched during business hours and the after-hours figure otherwise — unless the number of member-side findings on the same service account resolved in the 365 days ending on the day before the resolution date of the call being charged is below the schedule's courtesy allowance, in which case the call is not charged.
5. **Other findings.** Findings of cooperative side or no trouble found are never charged.
6. **Reference.** A trouble call charge's source is the trouble report it resolves.
7. **No outage credit.** The cooperative pays no outage credit for loss of service on any schedule.

### Decision table for a resolved call

| Report type | Crew finding | Member-side findings in the prior 365 days, against the allowance | Charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Line down or tree on the line | Any | — | None |
| Other trouble | Cooperative side | — | None |
| Other trouble | No trouble found | — | None |
| Other trouble | Member side | Below the allowance | None |
| Other trouble | Member side | At or above the allowance, dispatched in business hours | Business-hours trouble call charge |
| Other trouble | Member side | At or above the allowance, dispatched outside business hours | After-hours trouble call charge |

### Hypothetical example

A Schedule R member (allowance 1) whose blinking lights are traced to a loose connection in the member's own panel, with no member-side finding in the prior 365 days, is not charged. A second member-side finding four months later is charged at the figure for its dispatch period.
